title: Goose v2 Form
eyebrow: Design for approval · Models #19, muscle, sag, ribs under the skin and feathers over the joins · nothing changed in the model yet

short.lead: #19 gives the fused goose body the shape of a starved, living animal. You approved the list of changes in the goose model review, so this page covers how they fit. Only 2,180 triangles are left in the 300,000 budget, and the feathers over the joins alone cost 7,128. I ran a throwaway test that pays for them by turning the rib tubes and leg rings into the skin itself. Both rib options (ridges only, and ridges with bone breaking through) stayed inside the budget, and the skin stayed one piece. The pictures are untextured. Two questions follow.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it changes.
items: Muscle at the chest and shoulders, a sagging belly and folds at the neck root

Rounded masses melt into the skin: breast muscle either side of the neck root, shoulder muscle where each wing arm joins, and thigh muscle over each hip. A heavy belly hangs below the body. Three loose folds of skin wrap its base. All of it is part of the one skin, so it adds no triangles.

items.alt: Untextured test render of the chest with breast muscle, folds at the neck root and a sagging belly
items.caption: Throwaway test: chest muscle, neck folds and the belly.

items: Ribs pushing up under the skin
The 10 separate rib bones that sit on top of the flanks are replaced by ridges inside the skin, which frees 4,680 triangles. You choose whether bare bone also breaks through the middle of each rib.

items: 22 matted feathers (hackles) hang around the neck root, 9 short overlapping feathers (coverts) cover each wing shoulder, and 13 ragged feathers hang over each thigh. Together they cost 7,128 triangles.
Continuous scales instead of stacked rings
The five raised rings on each shank go, which frees 2,880 triangles. The continuous scale pattern is then painted in #20 (textures).

choices: A starved animal with the ribs straining against the skin. Total: 297,388 triangles.

choices.caption: Option A: ridges under the skin only.

choices: Ridges, with bare bone tearing through the middle
The middle third of each rib breaks out of the skin, matching the torn skin the review asked for. Total: 299,108 triangles, leaving 892.

choices.alt: Rib ridges with bone breaking through
choices.caption: Option B: ridges with bare bone tearing through the middle.

choices: I suggest option B (bone tearing through), because the approved review asked for torn skin and it matches the bone spikes you chose for the necks. It leaves only 892 triangles, so #20 (textures) and #21 (the rig) must add no new triangles.
When should the leg rings go?
The rings go in #19, and the legs look smooth until #20 paints the continuous scales.
The legs keep their rings for now, so the 2,880 triangles they would free stay used and the feathers no longer fit.
I suggest option A (remove them now), because the feathers over the joins only fit if the rings go.
